blocks.text: The chapter centers on Naaman, an Aramean military commander, who encounters Israel's prophet Elisha and is healed after following his instruction. This narrative demonstrates the God of Israel's power operating across political and national boundaries. Naaman's healing culminates in a significant confession: there is no God in all the earth except the God of Israel. This acknowledgment from a foreign military figure marks a turning point in the narrative, showing how divine power transcends expected boundaries and compels recognition from outside Israel's covenant community.
